'''Malcolm Ross O'Neill''' (born March 25, 1940) was the [[United States Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Logistics, and Technology]], having been sworn into office by [[United States Under Secretary of the Army]] [[Joseph W. Westphal]] on March 10, 2010,<ref name="army.mil">{{cite web |url=https://www.alt.army.mil/portal/page/portal/oasaalt/Bio_AAE |title=OASA(ALT) - Army Acquisition Executive (AAE) |accessdate=2011-01-06 |url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722220423/https://www.alt.army.mil/portal/page/portal/oasaalt/Bio_AAE |archivedate=2011-07-22}} Archived copy different from the original.</ref> and resigned June 3, 2011.<ref name="army.mil"/>

==Biography==
Source:<ref name="army.mil"/><ref name=resume>{{cite web |url=http://www.usasymposium.com/nano/05nano/oneill.htm |title=Resume of Service Career |date=1996-07-25 |access-date=2021-05-26}}</ref>

Malcolm Ross O'Neill was born in Chicago in 1940, where he graduated from [[Senn High School]] in 1958.<ref name="Senate bio">{{cite book |url=https://www.fas.org/irp/congress/2009_hr/nominate.pdf |title=Nominations Before the Senate Armed Services Committee, First Session, 111th Congress |date=2010 |pages=1535–1609 |publisher=U.S. Government Printing Office |location=Washington, D.C. |access-date=2021-05-26}}</ref> He was educated at [[DePaul University]], receiving a [[B.Sc.]] in [[Physics]].  In 1962, he joined the [[United States Army]] and was commissioned as a [[Field Artillery]] [[Officer (armed forces)|Officer]]. Following postings to [[Fort Sill]], [[Fort Benning]], [[Fort Bragg (North Carolina)|Fort Bragg]], [[Redstone Arsenal]], and the [[Defense Language Institute]] at the [[Presidio of Monterey, California|Presidio of Monterey]], O'Neill began his first tour of duty during the [[Vietnam War]] beginning in January 1965. There, he was posted at the [[Military Assistance Command, Vietnam]]. He spent 1966-67 as an instructor, and then [[aide-de-camp]] at Redstone Arsenal. In 1967-68, O'Neill was a student at the [[United States Army Ordnance Corps|United States Army Ordnance]] Center and School at [[Aberdeen Proving Ground]]. He then spent 1968-70 completing a [[master's degree]] in Physics at [[Rice University]]. He returned to Vietnam in June 1970, serving as Assistant Chief of Staff of the United States Army Support Command until June 1971. He then spent 1971-72 at the [[United States Army Command and General Staff College]], and then returned to Rice University, completing his [[Ph.D.]] in Physics in August 1974.

From 1974 to 1976, he was posted to the [[United States Army Missile Command]] at Redstone Arsenal. He then spent 1977 to 1980 at [[DARPA]]. After studying at the [[United States Army War College]] 1980-81, he spent 1981-83 in [[Munich]] as Deputy Program Manager of the [[NATO]] [[MIM-104 Patriot|Patriot]] Management Office.  He then spent the second half of 1983 as Chief of Staff of the United States Army Missile Command at Redstone Arsenal. In 1984, he was project manager for the [[M270 Multiple Launch Rocket System|Multiple Launch Rocket System]], posted at Redstone Arsenal. He spent 1985-87 as Director for [[Space weapon|Kinetic Energy Weapons]] in the [[Office of the Secretary of Defense]].

[[File:Portrait of U.S. Army Lt. Gen. Malcolm R. O'Neill.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Lt. Gen. O'Neill in 1993]]
From 1987 to 1989, O'Neill was commanding general of the [[United States Army Laboratory Command]] in [[Adelphi, Maryland]].  He worked in the Office of the [[Assistant Secretary of the Army (Research, Development and Acquisition)]] 1989-90, and was Deputy Director, then Acting Director, of the [[Strategic Defense Initiative Organization]] 1990-93. From 1993 to 1996, he was Director of the [[Ballistic Missile Defense Organization]]. O'Neill retired from the Army in 1996, having achieved the rank of [[Lieutenant general (United States)|Lieutenant General]].

In 1996, O'Neill joined [[Lockheed Martin]] as Vice President for Operations and Best Practices in the Space and Strategic Missiles Division. In 2000, he became Lockheed Martin's [[Chief Technical Officer]], a position he held until 2006.  He left Lockheed Martin in 2006, becoming Chairman of the [[United States National Academies]]'s Board on Army Science and Technology.

[[President of the United States]] [[Barack Obama]] nominated O'Neill to be [[United States Assistant Secretary of the Army for Acquisition, Logistics, and Technology]] in 2010, and O'Neill was sworn into office by [[United States Under Secretary of the Army]] [[Joseph W. Westphal]] on March 10, 2010, and resigned effective June 3, 2011.<ref name="army.mil"/>
